findings: Keep kafka-config responsible for Redpanda values and broker lifecycle.
Keep kafka-acls responsible for the standalone ACL reconciler and exact Deployment Controller policy.
Keep pve-infra responsible for Argo Applications, certificates, namespaces, and cluster wiring.
Do not base kafka-config on Codicarium's Strimzi Kafka platform repository; use the existing single-node Redpanda contract instead.
Preserve the existing StatefulSet, release, PVC, services, and TLS identities during source migration.
The original spec needed exact kubeconfig/API-server fail-closed targeting; the revised spec now names /home/rickebo/.kube/homelab.yaml, context default, and https://192.168.1.89:6443.
The revised spec adds phased migration, PVC preservation, prune/rollback controls, exact TLS/ACL policy evidence, repository-scoped credentials, and indirect dependency closure scanning.
No Kafka source may use Codicarium repositories or artifacts; public Redpanda upstream is permitted only as an explicitly approved chart source.
Live homelab Redpanda is StatefulSet redpanda 1/1 with a Bound 10 GiB local-path PVC and service ports 9093/9644.
Live Deployment Controller controller and webhook are both 2/2 Ready and use the local redpanda.deployment-controller.svc.cluster.local endpoint.
The current kafka ACL Argo Application is Unknown only because it points at codicarium/kafka-acls; replacing that source is the required cutover.
The current broker source uses public charts.redpanda.com and existing Redpanda values; the new Rickebo repo can own the values/wrapper without importing Codicarium Kafka configuration.
Manager-defined test plan covers repository CI, Helm/Argo render checks, explicit cluster preflight, live topics/ACLs, controller readiness, dependency closure, and guarded runner activation.

consensus: Proceed to implementation only with Rickebo-owned Kafka repositories, exact homelab target preflight, in-place broker/PVC migration, exact ACL proof, and fail-closed cross-organization dependency scanning.
open_risks: pve-infra is currently under the Rickebo account and its later transfer to rickebo-com remains a separate migration.
The Deployment Controller runtime artifact remains Codicarium-owned; this rollout removes only Kafka-related Codicarium dependencies as requested.

Existing controller topic names have Codicarium branding; the implementation must decide whether to preserve them for compatibility or rename before first managed ACL reconciliation, with no untracked data migration.
